conflicts.message: Specification narrative gives a 2014-byte example while Table 2 and implementation maximum give 2015 bytes; the structured reported/max value follows Table 2 and params.h, with the narrative discrepancy retained here.

The security discussion says the 128-bit profile is chosen for at least 160 classical bits before Grover, while the parameter-set label and call category are 128-bit classical; both scopes are retained.

The specification labels S/F as size/performance schedules, but the included single-run smoke benchmark does not uniformly make every F variant faster; claims are retained as design intent and benchmark caveat.

The clarification assigns GreatWall-192/256/512 to evaluation Levels 1/2/3 and treats GreatWall-128 as additional, while the main specification Table 3 labels NGCC levels differently; target bit strengths follow the cryptographic table.
Specification covers three instances but states the repository reference implementation currently realizes only Level-1.

The scheme calls the key compact relative to a dense explicit MQ key, but the serialized public key is still 2,996-35,924 bytes; this is retained as a qualified submitter claim and a parameter-derived constraint.

Phoenix-SHAKE-192s implementation macros give a 13,332-byte maximum while the SM3 parameter table reports 13,356 bytes and the SHAKE benchmark reports 13,290 bytes; these are preserved as maximum/reporting differences.
Several SHAKE benchmark sizes exceed the corresponding shared-profile implementation maxima (notably 256s/256f), suggesting backend/profile or reporting inconsistencies requiring cross-review.
QingLuan-128 reports binding_quantum_bits=64 under full Grover, below the stated 80-bit target, but separately claims Category 1 compliance under finite-depth Grover assumptions.
Package filenames for the basic-information form and specification appear swapped relative to their contents.
Abstract calls the iterative sampler rejection-free, while key generation rejects by norm and signing can restart on rANS overflow; both scopes are preserved.
The main specification describes Level2 as 160/80-bit, while the supplementary statement maps Level2 to the required 128/80-bit NGCC category; target_security follows the supplementary mapping.
Theoretical Table 1 sizes and actual serialized Table 3 sizes differ; structured sizes use actual API storage.
Narrative states 96-byte and 85-byte level-one signatures in different passages; Table 1 and structured value use 85 bytes.
